newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar slide plays havoc with gold punters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar slide plays havoc with gold punters.

text.p: Investors in the gold market who had bet on the metal plunging to fresh lows in the near future had their dreams shattered on Friday by the dollar's weakness.

In other commodity markets base metals remained volatile with Thursday's warning shot from London Metal Exchange (LME) authorities having little immediate impact on liquidity problems in zinc and aluminium markets.
The spot gold bullion price rose around $3 an ounce by the London close and quickly put on almost another $3 as the New York market continued the trend.
"The dollar slide is a big factor here, along with sharply lower equities prices, and it is forcing fund shortcovering," a New York trader said.
"Gold has been out of fashion for some time as a hedge against turmoil in the finanacial markets. But with the dollar, equities and bonds all looking sick, where else can you go." one analyst said.
The spot price ended London trading at around $324.85 an ounce and by 1730 GMT it moved on to around $327.00 an ounce in the New York market.

On the London Metal Exchange the refusal of certain strong holders of zinc to relieve the nearby supply bottlenecks saw the premium for spot metal over three months delivery surge 50 percent a tonne to around $150.

A European merchant and investment funds are believed to be controlling the market, with Chinese smelters having problems in meeting commitments against previously sold positions totalling aorund 250,000 tonnes.
On Thursday the LME said that it would not hesitate to take disciplinary procedures against members who create a disorderly market or other undesirable situations.
At least the tightness in aluminium supplies on the LME did not get any worse with the cash metal premium above three months holding around $15 a tonne, the same level as Thursday.

But traders pointed out that August markets are notoriously thin due to the absence of many particpants in the Northern Hemisphere on their summer holiday breaks, and that situations could change fairly rapidly.
